🇺🇸 🇨🇳 The US illegally issues deep-sea mining leases in efforts to compete with China The US has put its first-ever critical mineral mining lease up for auction, covering two areas spanning approximately 31.5 million acres off the coast of American Samoa, despite a ruling by a Hawaiian judge voiding the project’s environmental clearance. 🔊 “American manufacturers rely on critical minerals to build advanced electronics, energy infrastructure, and equipment for our national defense, but heavy reliance on overseas suppliers leaves manufacturers vulnerable when those supplies are disrupted,” Acting Marine Minerals Administration Director Mike Olsen said ahead of the auction. The bid, secured for $6 million by Wetstone US Ventures, aims to extract a range of critical minerals used in electronics manufacturing and defense systems, including: 🔴 Cobalt 🔴 Copper 🔴 Nickel 🔴 Manganese The two 20-year leases come after US President Donald Trump issued a directive last year to ramp up deep-sea mining to extract critical resources in an effort to compete with China. He also urged US agencies to expedite all related permitting. China currently controls approximately 70% of global critical mineral production, along with up to 90% of total refining and processing capacity, while the US remains dependent on imports for more than 50% of its annual consumption. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime

Denmark’s PM Mette Frederiksen on immigrants: I think many of us, many years ago when immigration began, thought: Okay, people are coming here. Some are fleeing, some are coming to work. Many came who do not like us, who do not like homosexuals, who do not agree with equality for women, who believe that their own religion, Islam, should stand above democracy. They use violence as a legitimate tool in raising their children, against women, and against others in the streets. And that dominance culture is dangerous. I say that as a Social Democrat, I say it as a woman, I say it as a Dane. But I also say it as prime minister of a country where that dominance culture is incompatible with the way we have built our society.

Icelandic hosting provider 1984, known for hosting independent media and activists, has gone completely offline, according to NetBlocks. The company has shut down its services after what it calls a "sophisticated and severe cyberattack". NetBlocks ( @netblocks ) ⚠️ Confirmed: Metrics show a loss of connectivity at free speech hosting provider 1984 in #Iceland , known for hosting independent media and activists. The incident comes as the company shuts down its services amid what it describes as a "sophisticated and severe cyberattack".
